text:
kai: quick flag from nivara-v1 int8 onboarding: small but consistent chrF/bleu hits on multilingual tests that mix CJK + invisible joiners (U+2060) and some legacy BOMs. looks like token seams are moving when joiners are present. :frowning:
sora: can you paste a minimal repro + tokens? which build changed for int8?
kai: sure, minimal case below. note FP16 vs INT8 detok diff.
```
Source: \u6771\u4eac\u2060\u00b7\u0627\u0644\u0623\u062e\u0628\u0627\u0631\u2014\u30ab\u30b9
FP16 detok: \u6771\u4eac\u30fb\u00b7\u0627\u0644\u0623\u062e\u0628\u0627\u0631\u2014\u30ab\u30b9
INT8 detok: \u6771\u4eac-\u30fb\u0627\u0644\u0623\u062e\u0628\u0627\u0631-\u30ab\u30b9
```
(kai: U+2060 word joiner vs explicit katakana middle dot mapping; em-dash vs hyphen mapping changed too)
ellen: tokenizer dump?
sora: ran the tokenizer harness on the exact bytes. FP16 tokens: ["\u6771","\u4eac","\u2060","\u00b7","\u0627...","\u2014","\u30ab","\u30b9"] INT8 tokens: ["\u6771","\u4eac","-","\u30fb","\u0627...","-","\u30ab","\u30b9"]
so the word-joiner got collapsed into a seam at a different boundary and a middle-dot vs katakana-dot mapping toggled. that changes token ids before decoding.
jun: FYI int8 rollout included a compact tokenizer artifact and a switch to a newer SPM packer that changed how invisible joiners are canonicalized in the binary. both could be factors.
ci-bot: smoke-run nivara-v1-int8 4950002280: bleu_base=23.7, bleu_int8=20.1, chrf_base=0.638, chrf_int8=0.596, regression_count=502, top-pattern="wordjoiner-seam-shift"
kai: hypothesis: (A) artifact-level canonicalization mismatch for U+2060/ZWSP/FEFF vs runtime normalizer; (B) compacted tokenizer reorders mapping table so tie-break rules pick different subtokens when invisible chars present.
ellen: immediate mitigation: canonicalize joiners and punctuation at ingress to a stable set before tokenization. map U+2060 -> U+200D (ZWJ) or drop to space? need to decide. also normalize BOMs -> remove or replace. log counts.
sora: I prototyped canonicalizer that normalizes NFKC then explicitly normalizes joiners and mid-dots:
```
# prototype
s = unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', s)
s = s.replace('\uFEFF', '')  # drop BOM
s = s.replace('\u2060', '\u200D')  # canonicalize word-joiner -> ZWJ
s = s.replace('\u00B7', '\u30FB')  # middle dot -> katakana mid dot
s = s.replace('\u2014', '-')
```
ran local mini-bench: tokens align across fp16/int8 for canonicalized inputs and chrF recovers ~0.025 on the slice.
jun: We should be conservative with replacing invisible controls. Some customers use joiners intentionally. Proposal: add a feature flag tokenize.canonicalize_invisibles with default off, run canary on 3% int8 traffic. also emit a metric of replaced_joiners per-1k to monitor potential data loss.
kai: add unit tests: tests/locale/word_joiner_fixtures.txt with 30 edge cases mixing CJK+RTL+joiners+BOMs and assert token ids identical post-canonicalization across fp16/int8.
elllen: small ops note: ensure hosted and private build pipelines include the canonicalizer code in the tokenizer artifact so private deployments can opt-in. sync SDK docs.
ci-bot: canary-plan created 4950002295 -> route 3% int8 traffic with canonicalizer=true, collect BLEU/chrF and token-dump traces.
sora: owners: sora -> canonicalizer PR + fixtures, kai -> coord canary & metrics, jun -> tokenizer artifact build-verifier. will push PR with tests today.
kai: if canonicalization fails to recover >90% regressions we escalate to unpacking compact-tokenizer serializer and SPM tie-break heuristics. thanks all, keep short updates here. :rocket:
